classification.difficultyReason: Students must construct a joint event by subtraction and distinguish two conditional sample spaces when sampling without replacement.

content.prompt: A box contains 35 apples, of which 25 are red and 10 are green. Of the red apples, five contain an insect and of the green apples, one contains an insect. Two apples are chosen at random from the box. Find the probability that:

children.label: a
children.prompt: both apples are red and at least one contains an insect

answer.worked:
There are 20 red apples without insects. Subtract the probability of two insect-free red apples from that of two red apples.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{both red, at least one insect})&=\frac{25}{35}\times\frac{24}{34}-\frac{20}{35}\times\frac{19}{34}\\P(\text{both red, at least one insect})&=\frac{220}{1190}\\P(\text{both red, at least one insect})&=\frac{22}{119}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: at least one apple contains an insect given that both apples are red

answer.worked:
Restrict the sample space to the 25 red apples, of which 20 contain no insect.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{at least one insect}\mid\text{both red})&=1-\frac{20}{25}\times\frac{19}{24}\\P(\text{at least one insect}\mid\text{both red})&=\frac{11}{30}\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: both apples are red given that at least one is red

answer.worked:
Let $R$ mean both apples are red and $E$ mean at least one is red. Since $R\subseteq E$,
$$\begin{align*}P(E)&=1-\frac{10}{35}\times\frac{9}{34}=\frac{1100}{1190}\\P(R)&=\frac{25}{35}\times\frac{24}{34}=\frac{600}{1190}\\P(R\mid E)&=\frac{600/1190}{1100/1190}\\P(R\mid E)&=\frac{6}{11}\end{align*}$$
